Resolves #20072

A dock strip now parks its within-toolbar reorder while the pointer is beyond its release band (`dockReleaseTolerance`, the band the release already voids on), so a tab dragged far from its strip no longer slides its siblings across it. Entering that territory walks the tracked switches back to the resting order; back inside the band the reorder resumes from the live pointer. The policy is `TabSortZone#updateReorderPark`, gated on `enableCrossZoneDrag` like the release. The base `SortZone` gains one default-off class field, `isReorderParked`, which `onDragMove` honours after its window-boundary sampling, so plain tab strips (`examples/tab/container`), maximized dock strips and the grid header keep following a loose hand. The drag trace records `park` / `unpark`.

No consumer lines to delete: the release void stays the authority, since a release can land beyond the band right after an in-band move, and the park only previews it.

Evidence: L2 (unit over real zones + NL e2e under a 4× CPU throttle, both red-first on `origin/dev`) → L3 required for AC-5 (the operator's live gesture). Residual: AC-5, Residual-Owner: #20022.

| AC-3 | CI-covered: same file › both "keeps following a loose hand beyond its boundary" arms (the `examples/tab/container` zone, a maximized dock strip); the grid header and the existing reorder arms run the unchanged base path |

## Deltas from ticket
- Ledger row 4 has the in-window park reuse the tear-out seam; it cannot: `isWindowDragging` short-circuits through `checkWindowBoundary`, which runs only with `enableProxyToPopup`, and it also gates the commit. The base gets its own `isReorderParked`, a class field rather than a config because it is per-gesture internal state (`src/core/Base.mjs` class-field contract), reset with `isWindowDragging` at drag end.
- The park restores the resting order itself: `startWindowDrag` only stops further switches, it never returned the siblings (intake comment on #20072). The walk-back reuses `switchItems`, which undoes itself for a neighbour pair.
- `park` / `unpark` trace events, so `get_drag_trace` shows the hover's decision.
- The `#19986` `onDragMove` stub gained the field and method the real class now carries; its assertions are unchanged.
- From Julia's review (non-blocking challenge), fixed here rather than ticketed: the park also clears `SortZone`'s duplicate-move guard. A scripted return to the last in-band pixel used to be swallowed as a duplicate, so its in-band release committed no reorder where dev commits the swap. The Workstation tours drive scripted gestures.

## Test Evidence
- Red-first on `origin/dev` `2bbedf0222` (a separate worktree carrying only the specs): the three dock unit arms fail on behaviour (a `switch` 300 px below the strip, twice; Audit left in the first slot after leaving the band); both control arms pass. Head: 48/48.
- The scripted re-entry arm: red on `01bd2b758e` (two switches, the re-entry sample swallowed, no commit), green on `0fb6cc852b`. `WorkstationTabDragSiblingHoldsNL` green again on `0fb6cc852b`.
- `WorkstationTabDragSiblingHoldsNL` (4× CPU throttle, Brain `dev` `97d3c695`): on dev, Audit's header took 32 distinct x positions while the pointer swept below the band; on head, one, and Metrics docks into the scale zone.
- Neighbouring dock-drag e2e on head (single worker): 43 passed across 17 files, every `e2e/workstation` tab-drag, cross-zone, overflow and popup spec plus `DemoBDockTearOutNL`, `DockCrossZoneDragNL`, `DockDragDropNL` and `DockOperationsNL`.
- Full unit suite on head: 5463 passed, 1 failed, 2 skipped. The red is `unit/e2e/browserLifecycleReporter.spec.mjs:256`, unrelated: its `not.toContain('4101')` scans the whole receipt, whose `loadAverage` read `11.041015625` on that run; alone it is 11/11 on base and head. Out of scope, noted in defect-note `MESSAGE:b4872f91-453a-4a2e-b91c-acdb204da24c`.
- agent-preflight: not hosted here; `check-ticket-archaeology` and `check-file-sizes --base origin/dev` ran clean, `check-pr-body` on this body.

### 🔬 Depth Floor

- **Challenge**: In `SortZone#onDragMove` (`src/draggable/container/SortZone.mjs` `L771-L777`), the duplicate-delivery guard (`if (!isOverDragging && clientX === me.lastInBoundX && clientY === me.lastInBoundY) return`) remembers the last pre-park `(lastInBoundX, lastInBoundY)` across a park/unpark cycle because `if (me.isReorderParked) return` exits at `L742` before `lastInBoundX/Y` are updated. If a scripted test or caller moves in-band to `(x1, y1)` (triggering a swap), parks outside the band at `(x1, y2)` (which mutates `itemRects` back to `startIndex`), and then re-enters at the exact same pixel `(x1, y1)` on its first in-band sample, `L771` will classify `(x1, y1)` as a duplicate (`t: 'dup'`) until the next pixel move. Non-blocking for live pointer streams (which continuously vary coordinates on re-entry), and if ever needed for scripted waypoint tests, `updateReorderPark` can clear `me.lastInBoundX = me.lastInBoundY = null` when walking switches back.
